title: Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP): Tenant-Wide License Cap per Plan
content:
**Cap clause.** On Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP), the licenses of one plan held by the tenant, plus the licenses being added, may never exceed the plan's most licenses per tenant. A plan marked unlimited has no cap.

- The licenses held are counted across all the tenant's subscriptions of that plan whose status is provisioning, active or suspended. They are counted at one point in time, immediately before the new subscription or seat addition being decided.
- Licenses on expired or cancelled subscriptions do not count toward the cap.

**Effect.** A new subscription or seat addition that would pass the cap cannot be placed, in whole or in part. The users beyond the cap must be licensed on a plan without a cap. The cap figure for each plan is in the plan ordering schedule.

## Judgement table

| Licenses held of the plan, plus licenses being added | Plan's cap | Can the order be placed? |
|---|---|---|
| Not more than the cap | a figure | Yes |
| More than the cap | a figure | No, not even the part that would fit |
| Any number | unlimited | Yes, there is no cap |

## Worked cases (hypothetical holdings, on a plan capped at 300)

1. A tenant has 250 licenses of the plan on an active subscription and 30 on a suspended one. A seat addition of 20 brings the total to 300, which does not exceed 300, so it can be placed.
2. The same tenant asks for 21. The total would be 301, so the seat addition of 21 cannot be placed, not even in part. The users beyond the cap must be licensed on a plan without a cap.
3. A third subscription of the plan with 100 licenses expired last quarter. Those 100 are not counted.
